name: Complicity
overview: Scripture reveals complicity as a serious moral failing where individuals share in the guilt of wrongdoing by consenting or partnering with sin, as seen in Psalms 50:18 and Proverbs 29:24. The New Testament provides concrete examples, such as the daughter of Herodias boldly requesting John the Baptist's execution (Matthew 14:8; Mark 6:25) and Pilate’s involvement in Jesus’ death through his reluctant but decisive role (Matthew 27:17; Mark 15:9). These instances highlight how complicity extends beyond passive observation to active participation or enabling of injustice.
